intelligence.enrichment: Sedimentation is the settling down of a heavier insoluble component at the bottom of a liquid, and decantation is removing the liquid by tilting the vessel. Leaving the mixture undisturbed lets the heavier insoluble part settle or a separate layer form, then tilting pours off the upper liquid. The learner correctly applies this rule: Sedimentation is the settling down of a heavier insoluble component at the bottom of a liquid, and decantation is removing the liquid by tilting the vessel. If a liquid is poured gently, any solid impurity in it is completely removed.
